source.title: The Geometry of Ignorance: Detecting Suppressed Knowledge in LLMs through Activation Fragmentation
source.authors: Adar Peleg; Dvir Alsheich; Tomer Ashuach; Avi Mendelson

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present. Some tables are flattened, but the listed GA, DPO, and RMU values used below can be assigned to their conditions from the table layout.
record.tranche_reason: It applies several unlearning methods and post-unlearning recovery attacks, but its main measurement is activation geometry and its correlations with attack outcomes rather than a direct reproduction of the original studies’ recovery measurements.
record.gate_note: The paper runs activation steering, five-shot ICL, and GCG after unlearning and reports attack scores. It also reports Forget ROUGE-L for unlearned checkpoints. Its discussion cites recovery findings from other work; those cited results are not recorded as rows. MIA results are not included because they do not measure one of the listed claim versions.
record.test_reason: The study applies six unlearning methods (GA, DPO, NPO, NPO+KL, RMU, WHP) to three 7–8B chat models on three concepts, then runs activation steering, five-shot ICL, GCG and MIA and reports attack success per run (Tables 13–15). These results bear directly on whether internal edits (C) or prompting (E) recover unlearned knowledge. The main contribution, a geometric fragmentation metric, is a different method aimed at the same suppression-vs-deletion question.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors also state that ICL is the only attack predicted robustly (LOO-stable and BH-significant); steering, GCG and MIA correlations are weaker or not significant. They read GA/DPO as suppressing outputs while leaving internal geometry intact, and RMU as distorting but not erasing it.
record.recipe_differences: Evaluates GA, DPO, NPO, NPO+KL, RMU, and Who’s Harry Potter-style redirection against activation steering, ICL, GCG, and MIA; adds activation-fragmentation measurements and attack-correlation analyses rather than reproducing a single original method.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcomes vary by unlearning method, model family, target concept, and attack. The paper reports attack-specific layer correlations and states that GA is the only method consistently bringing Steering AUC near chance across all three models; ICL aggregate deltas are near zero, and LLaMA-3 GCG accuracy is 0 under every method.

fits_no_version.finding: Anon-vector fragmentation metrics separate known (HP, Star Wars) from unknown (TOFU) concepts across 10 LLMs. Post-unlearning fragmentation correlates with ICL recoverability (ρ≈−0.51) and, via entropy metrics, with GCG and steering.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Representation geometry after unlearning predicts adversarial recoverability without running attacks.

record.peer_reviewed: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
record.problems: The paper notes limited concept coverage, English-only evaluation, deterministic anonymisation artifacts, and a correlational explanation for opposite attack/geometry trends that is not validated against generations or reasoning traces. RQ2 attack correlations use small subsets (n=44–45 aggregate; smaller layerwise subsets), and several runs are incomplete. The paper does not report targeted-knowledge accuracy against chance for the listed GA conditions.
record.rows_left_out: Within the 60-row limit, omitted most DPO ICL conditions, DPO GCG results, RMU GCG results, all NPO and NPO+KL attack rows, detailed Base rows, and MIA results. These are in Tables 13–15; the selected rows prioritize GA outcomes, activation-steering comparisons, and representative ICL comparisons. MIA is not one of the listed claim versions.

untested.parts: Targeted-knowledge accuracy vs chance; general-capability benchmarks per run (only a retain ROUGE-L ≥0.8× base criterion). Base forget ROUGE-L is already 0.06–0.15, so ROUGE-L cannot show chance-level forgetting.
Direction ablation not tested; only additive anon-vector steering.
Rephrasing, other languages and other jailbreaks not tested; only 5-shot ICL and answer-targeted GCG.

missing.what: Geometry analysis: GA on LLaMA-3 reaches Forget ROUGE-L 0.000 yet leaves AUSS/centroid norm near Base. GA and DPO leave concept geometry intact; RMU shifts it but does not erase it. This bears on C's 'blocks rather than deletes'.
missing.locator: Section 5 'Suppression versus deletion'; Tables 13–15 geometry columns

missing.what: WHP (Who's Harry Potter reimplementation) steering AUC is 0.71–0.92 on all models, with GCG 0.000.

record.verdict_notes: The reader misaligned Table 13/14 columns: the RMU steering and ICL rows carry WHP values, and two DPO LLaMA-2 steering values are NPO's. The record's method_sensitivity repeats the Figure 2 caption that LLaMA-3 GCG is 0 under every method, but Table 14 shows DPO 0.4/0.8 and NPO, NPO+KL and RMU at 1.0; the caption is contradicted by the table. Base GCG is 0.000 and Base steering AUC is below 0.5, so these measures may not register knowledge even in unmodified models. GCG targets the reference answer's first 8 tokens, inflating success. Sample sizes are small (25 steering/ICL pairs, 5 GCG pairs). GA's steered word frequency of 0.000 suggests model degeneration rather than clean forgetting. The Qwen table has one missing run (likely RMU HP). No A label is given because Forget ROUGE-L cannot show chance-level accuracy.

versions.untested_parts: It reports Forget ROUGE-L and attack outcomes, but not targeted-knowledge accuracy against a chance baseline. Retain ROUGE-L is used as a verification criterion; this extraction does not record every retain score.
No recovery by fine-tuning on unrelated, loosely related, or forgotten-fact training examples is tested; ICL is prompting, not fine-tuning.
Activation steering is tested as an internal recovery intervention, and the paper analyzes representation geometry. Ablating an activation direction is not tested.
Five-shot ICL and GCG suffix prompting are tested. Rephrasing-only prompts, other languages, and other jailbreak methods are not tested.
The paper does not test a newer method specifically claiming to resist the listed attacks.

statements.correction: Steering AUC: DPO 0.620-0.911, RMU 0.694-0.896 (LLaMA-2/3; Qwen RMU 0.784/0.634 in text, not in rows); Base 0.423-0.503. Models: LLaMA-2-7B-chat and Meta-LLaMA-3-8B-Instruct (LLaMA family) and Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, so two families. Corrected values: RMU L3 0.896/0.854/0.766 (rows hold WHP 0.922/0.846/0.850); DPO L2 SW/WS 0.673/0.658 (rows hold NPO 0.668/0.795).
statements.problem: Steering range and Base reference are right with corrected values. But the 'why' says 'three model families': the RQ2 unlearning models are three models from two families. The paper's three families (Qwen, Gemma, LLaMA) refer to the ten RQ1 models. Also, the note on wrong rows covers only RMU-S-L2-*, but RMU-S-L3-* and DPO-S-L2-SW/WS also hold other methods' cells.

statements.correction: The paper says GA 'consistently drives Steer-AUC near chance'. GA: Steer-WF 0.000, forget ROUGE-L 0.000, no retain regularisation (Appendix B.5). Output degeneration is the catalog's reading, not the authors'.
statements.problem: Numbers are right. But differences_stated says 2611.05272 'notes that GA output degeneration may explain the null'. The paper never mentions degeneration. That caveat comes from the catalog verdict (l1), not the authors.

statements.correction: Meta-LLaMA-3-8B-Instruct 5-shot ICL delta: GA +0.000 on HP, SW, WS; RMU -0.040 (HP), +0.040 (SW), +0.040 (WS).
